assertion.statement: For C:y^2=x^3-(3-sqrt2)^2*x over K0=Q(sqrt2), every P in C(K0) satisfies 2*hhat(P)=lim_j 4^(-j)*h_x([2^j]P).
assertion.objects: The actual curve C, its degree-two x-map to P1, absolute logarithmic projective x-height and Silverman canonical height.
assertion.hypotheses: K0 is a number field; C is a nonsingular elliptic curve; h_x includes every place with normalization 1/[K0:Q].
assertion.quantifiers: Every P in C(K0), including the identity and torsion; limit over nonnegative integers j.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed characteristic-zero curve C, delta=3-sqrt2 nonzero.
assertion.uniformity: The same canonical-height convention is used at every iterate; no point-dependent rescaling.
assertion.constants: The factor2 is deg(x). No numerical duplication error bound is supplied by this theorem.
assertion.normalizations: Silverman second edition definition following VIII Proposition9.1; the convention is hhat=(1/deg f)*lim4^(-j)h_f([2^j]P), not the doubled convention noted in Remark9.2.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The projective x-map sends the identity to infinity, of height0; doubling into the identity remains covered. No nontorsion assumption is needed for the limit identity.
assertion.limit_order: Fix C, P and the absolute height, iterate doubling, then take j to infinity.

supplier.statement: For an elliptic curve E over a number field and any nonconstant even rational function f, (1/deg f)*lim_j 4^(-j)*h_f([2^j]P) exists for every algebraic point P and defines the canonical height independently of f.
